prompt: There is a bug report in ISSUE.md. Fix the code in this folder so the issue is resolved. Do not ask questions; make the fix.
final_response:
Fixed `from_roman()` in `roman.py`.

The original implementation blindly summed/negated character values with no validation, so it accepted garbage like `'IIII'`, `'VX'`, `'IC'`, `'XM'`, `'VV'`, and `'MMMM'`.

The fix:
- Uppercases input so lowercase (`'xiv'`) is accepted.
- Validates the input against a regex for standard subtractive-form Roman numerals 1–3999 (`M{0,3}(CM|CD|D?C{0,3})(XC|XL|L?X{0,3})(IX|IV|V?I{0,3})`), rejecting empty/non-string/invalid input with `ValueError`.
- Then applies the original subtractive summation only to validated numerals.

Verified against all the required cases plus additional edge cases (valid `'XIV'=14`, `'MCMXCIV'=1994`, `'MMMCMXCIX'=3999`, `'xiv'=14`; invalid `'IIII'`, `'VX'`, `'IC'`, `'XM'`, `'VV'`, `'MMMM'`, `''`, and others).
